title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授宋　批〔論以心學立說卓有定見且筆陣滔滔閫閫　變化出奇縱横真可謂倒流三峽水掃千人軍也者其如是安得不為之表彰〕
居天下之上而有先天下之見明矣哉天
子之心也蓋心明則見明見明則智邁群
倫而人莫能測其機神遊物表而人莫能
窺其妙矣不明其心則蔽於欲而昧於理
雖近在目前之事尚莫能見况萬里之外
乎光武預測竇融之將附遂授璽書於河
西以迎之人皆駭異以為天子明見萬里
===
之外嗚呼光武其真出尋常萬萬者乎夫
天子中天下而立定四海之民受天明命
而奄有九有膺天曆數而誕受多方九夷
八蠻皆臣妾也六服群辟皆藩籬也無一
地而不歸於總括之中無一民而不在於
範圍之内天地之所覆載日月之所照臨
與夫舟車之所至人力之所通何者而非
天子之所統乎夫以天下之大如此道里
之遠如此山川之間隔疆域之遼邈又如
punctuated:
考試官教授宋，批〔論以心學立說，卓有定見，且筆陣滔滔，閫閫，變化出奇，縱横真可謂倒流三峽水，掃千人軍也者。其如是，安得不為之表彰？〕

居天下之上，而有先天下之見，明矣哉，天子之心也！蓋心明則見明，見明則智邁群倫，而人莫能測其機；神遊物表，而人莫能窺其妙矣。不明其心，則蔽於欲而昧於理，雖近在目前之事，尚莫能見，况萬里之外乎？光武預測竇融之將附，遂授璽書於河西以迎之，人皆駭異，以為天子明見萬里之外。嗚呼！光武其真出尋常萬萬者乎！夫天子中天下而立，定四海之民，受天明命而奄有九有，膺天曆數而誕受多方。九夷八蠻皆臣妾也，六服群辟皆藩籬也。無一地而不歸於總括之中，無一民而不在於範圍之内。天地之所覆載，日月之所照臨，與夫舟車之所至，人力之所通，何者而非天子之所統乎？夫以天下之大如此，道里之遠如此，山川之間隔、疆域之遼邈又如
translation_en:
Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: 〔This discourse grounds its argument in the learning of the mind and displays remarkably firm convictions. Moreover, its ranks of words surge forth in torrents, “kun kun” [?], producing surprising transformations. In its sweeping power it may truly be said to “reverse the waters of the Three Gorges and sweep away an army of a thousand men.” With such qualities, how could one fail to give it recognition?〕

Occupying the highest position in the world, yet possessing insight ahead of all the world—how luminous is the mind of the Son of Heaven! When the mind is clear, perception is clear; when perception is clear, wisdom surpasses that of all others, and none can fathom its workings. His spirit roams beyond outward things, and none can glimpse its subtleties. If he does not illuminate his mind, he is blinded by desire and ignorant of principle. He cannot discern even matters immediately before his eyes, much less those ten thousand li away! Guangwu foresaw that Dou Rong would offer his allegiance, and accordingly sent an imperially sealed letter to Hexi to welcome him. Everyone was astonished, believing that the Son of Heaven clearly perceived what lay beyond ten thousand li. Ah! Did Guangwu truly surpass ordinary men ten thousand times over?

The Son of Heaven stands at the center of the world and settles the people within the Four Seas. Receiving Heaven’s luminous mandate, he possesses all the Nine Regions; receiving Heaven’s appointed succession, he takes charge of the many lands. The Nine Yi and Eight Man peoples are all his subjects and servants; the many rulers of the Six Zones of Allegiance are all his protective barriers. No territory lies outside his comprehensive dominion, and no person falls beyond its bounds. Wherever Heaven covers and Earth sustains, wherever the sun and moon shine, wherever boats and carriages reach and human effort opens passage—what place is not governed by the Son of Heaven? Yet with the world so vast, its distances so great, and the separation imposed by mountains and rivers and the remoteness of its territories likewise so…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
此天子拱五位之上處九重之邃天陛其
沉沉也君門其遼遼也環堵之外足迹猶
有所未至蕭牆之內目力猶有所未及欲
見萬里之外豈不難乎見且難況欲察人
心向背於未然而應之得其當者豈不為
尤難乎自其難而求其所以易其必有所
本矣且人之一心所以具衆理而應萬事
者也茍一事不照以此心則無以決可否
於一事處一家不照以此心則無以措條
===
理於一家理一國不照以此心則無以判
安危於一國況治天下之大者乎是以天
子知心不可以不明也存之於至靜養之
於至微私欲蔽吾心也而去之聲色蠱吾
心也而去之貨利迷吾心也而去之讒佞
賊吾心也而去之珎奇玩好又搖蕩吾心
也而去之孔子曰操則存吾何為而或舍
孟子曰求放心吾何為而或失吾之神明
也何為而使其不靈吾之主宰也何為而
punctuated: 此。天子拱五位之上，處九重之邃，天陛其沉沉也，君門其遼遼也。環堵之外，足迹猶有所未至；蕭牆之內，目力猶有所未及。欲見萬里之外，豈不難乎？見且難，況欲察人心向背於未然，而應之得其當者，豈不為尤難乎？自其難而求其所以易，其必有所本矣。且人之一心，所以具衆理而應萬事者也。茍一事不照以此心，則無以決可否於一事；處一家不照以此心，則無以措條理於一家；理一國不照以此心，則無以判安危於一國。況治天下之大者乎？是以天子知心不可以不明也。存之於至靜，養之於至微。私欲蔽吾心也，而去之；聲色蠱吾心也，而去之；貨利迷吾心也，而去之；讒佞賊吾心也，而去之；珎奇玩好又搖蕩吾心也，而去之。孔子曰：「操則存。」吾何為而或舍？孟子曰：「求放心。」吾何為而或失？吾之神明也，何為而使其不靈？吾之主宰也，何為而
translation_en: …thus. The Son of Heaven sits with hands folded in the exalted fifth position, dwelling in the depths of the ninefold palace. How imposing are the imperial steps; how remote the sovereign’s gates! Beyond his enclosing walls there are places his footsteps have never reached; even within the palace screen wall there are places his eyes cannot reach. Would it not be difficult to see ten thousand li away? If even seeing is difficult, how much more difficult must it be to discern, before it becomes manifest, whether people’s hearts will turn toward him or away, and to respond appropriately? If we seek what can make this difficulty easy, there must surely be a foundation upon which it rests. A person’s single mind embodies the many principles and responds to the myriad affairs. If even one matter is not illuminated by this mind, there is no means of deciding what is acceptable or unacceptable in that matter. If, in managing a household, one does not illuminate it with this mind, there is no means of establishing order in that household. If, in governing a state, one does not illuminate it with this mind, there is no means of judging the state’s security or peril. How much more is this so when governing all the vast realm under Heaven! Thus the Son of Heaven knows that his mind must be clear. He preserves it in utmost stillness and nurtures it in its subtlest workings. Selfish desires obscure my mind, so I remove them; music and sensual beauty bewitch my mind, so I remove them; wealth and profit delude my mind, so I remove them; slander and flattery injure my mind, so I remove them; rare treasures and prized amusements unsettle my mind, so I remove them. Confucius said, “Hold fast to it, and it remains.” Why should I ever let it go? Mencius said, “Seek the mind that has strayed.” Why should I ever lose it? It is my spiritual intelligence: why should I allow it to become unresponsive? It is my governing master: why should I…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
使其不正吾之嚴師也何爲而使其不安
止水也何爲而使其揚波明鑑也何爲而
使其積塵夫然則一理融萬理徹一塵淨
萬境新靈臺湛然而此心明矣見其有不
明者乎是以智足以審天下之先幾膚足
以通天下之萬務是非也而能決之賢否
也而能辨之善惡也而能分之安危利害
也而能審之向背從違也而能察之咫尺
之間萬里之外遠近不同也一明見之流
===
通殿陛之前海隅之地內外不一也一明
見之周徹黈纊塞耳不用其聰而聰自周
於九圍冕旒蔽目不用其明而明已照於
萬里視八荒如朝宁華夏都邑洞然我闥
也覩萬里如庭階四海九州瞭然一腔也
不必乘輿之徧歷也而生民之休戚皆歸
於容光必照之中不必萬乘之四巡也而
遠人之叛服皆在於無幽不燭之下蕩蕩
乎配天地而咸宜炯炯乎並日月而無二
punctuated: 使其不正？吾之嚴師也，何爲而使其不安？止水也，何爲而使其揚波？明鑑也，何爲而使其積塵？夫然，則一理融，萬理徹；一塵淨，萬境新。靈臺湛然，而此心明矣，見其有不明者乎？是以智足以審天下之先幾，膚足以通天下之萬務。是非也，而能決之；賢否也，而能辨之；善惡也，而能分之；安危利害也，而能審之；向背從違也，而能察之。咫尺之間，萬里之外，遠近不同也，一明見之流通；殿陛之前，海隅之地，內外不一也，一明見之周徹。黈纊塞耳，不用其聰，而聰自周於九圍；冕旒蔽目，不用其明，而明已照於萬里。視八荒如朝宁，華夏都邑，洞然我闥也；覩萬里如庭階，四海九州，瞭然一腔也。不必乘輿之徧歷也，而生民之休戚皆歸於容光必照之中；不必萬乘之四巡也，而遠人之叛服皆在於無幽不燭之下。蕩蕩乎，配天地而咸宜；炯炯乎，並日月而無二。
translation_en: …allow it to become improper? It is my stern teacher: why should I allow it to become unsettled? It is still water: why should I let waves disturb it? It is a bright mirror: why should I let dust accumulate upon it? When this is so, one principle is fully comprehended and all principles become clear; one speck of dust is cleared away and every realm is renewed. The mind’s spiritual terrace is limpid, and this heart is illuminated. Can anything in it be found that is not clear? Thus his wisdom suffices to discern the earliest stirrings of affairs throughout the realm, and his capacity [?] suffices to comprehend its myriad concerns. He can settle questions of right and wrong, distinguish the worthy from the unworthy, separate good from evil, assess security and danger, benefit and harm, and discern allegiance and opposition, obedience and defiance. Whether within inches or ten thousand li away, distances differ, yet a single illumination is seen to flow through them all. Whether before the palace steps or at the edges of the seas, inner and outer regions differ, yet a single illumination is seen to penetrate them completely. Yellow floss pendants stop his ears: he does not employ his hearing, yet his hearing naturally encompasses all nine regions. The pendant strings of his ceremonial crown screen his eyes: he does not employ his sight, yet his illumination already shines over ten thousand li. He views the eight distant reaches as though they were his court; the cities of the Chinese realm lie as plainly before him as his own doorway. He beholds ten thousand li as though they were his courtyard steps; all within the four seas and the nine provinces is as clear to him as the interior of his own breast. His imperial carriage need not travel everywhere for all the joys and sorrows of the people to fall within the illumination that reaches even the smallest opening. The lord of ten thousand chariots need not tour the four quarters for the rebellion or submission of distant peoples to lie beneath a light that leaves no dark recess unlit. Vast indeed, he matches Heaven and Earth and is fitting in all things; radiant indeed, he stands beside the sun and moon, no different from them.

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
天子何以得此亦惟極心體之明耳昌
抑觀諸光武之事乎光武以明識之資撥
炎劉之運斯時也有若竇融之在河西知
其無可注足之地也而歸漢之心以興知
其無可事尚之主也而附劉之念以萌光
武預覘於未動之先逆料於既萌之後不
待覲王庭而敷奏以言也藩垣之寄遂授
不待趨帝闕而明試以功也保障之任遂
托詔旨親頒肅肅乎帝語之丁寧天恩誕
===
及煌煌乎玉音之炫燿不流盼於萬里而
人心之所嚮無不知不揚眉於四方而人
心之所從無不見是何也蓋必有以極此
心之體無不明故照天下之事而無遠不
屆耳彼河西之人但見萬里之外事未舉
而先知機將萌而遂應為可駭可愕而已
孰知其本於此哉噫此光武所以振中興
之治功復高仁之故物而謂之明君也歟
世之求細故察秋毫照淵魚以為明者特
punctuated: 天子何以得此？亦惟極心體之明耳。昌，抑觀諸光武之事乎？光武以明識之資，撥炎劉之運。斯時也，有若竇融之在河西，知其無可注足之地也，而歸漢之心以興；知其無可事尚之主也，而附劉之念以萌。光武預覘於未動之先，逆料於既萌之後，不待覲王庭而敷奏以言也，藩垣之寄遂授；不待趨帝闕而明試以功也，保障之任遂托。詔旨親頒，肅肅乎帝語之丁寧；天恩誕及，煌煌乎玉音之炫燿。不流盼於萬里，而人心之所嚮無不知；不揚眉於四方，而人心之所從無不見。是何也？蓋必有以極此心之體，無不明，故照天下之事，而無遠不屆耳。彼河西之人，但見萬里之外，事未舉而先知，機將萌而遂應，為可駭可愕而已，孰知其本於此哉？噫！此光武所以振中興之治功，復高仁之故物，而謂之明君也歟？世之求細故、察秋毫、照淵魚以為明者，特
translation_en: How does the Son of Heaven attain this? Simply by fully realizing the luminosity inherent in the mind. Chang [?]—might we also examine this in the deeds of Guangwu? Endowed with clear discernment, Guangwu restored the fortunes of the Liu dynasty, associated with the virtue of Fire. At that time, there was Dou Rong in Hexi: recognizing that he had nowhere to establish a footing, he conceived the desire to return to the Han; recognizing that he had no ruler whom he could serve and esteem, he began to consider allegiance to the Liu house. Guangwu perceived his intentions before he acted and anticipated their course once they had begun to form. Without waiting for him to appear at the royal court and state his case, he entrusted him with the charge of serving as a defensive bulwark; without waiting for him to hasten to the imperial palace and demonstrate his merit through achievements, he assigned him responsibility for protection and defense. The edict was personally issued: solemn indeed were the emperor’s earnest injunctions. Imperial favor extended far and wide: resplendent indeed was the brilliance of his august words. Without casting his gaze across ten thousand li, he knew every inclination of men’s hearts; without raising his eyes toward the four quarters, he saw every allegiance they embraced. Why was this? Surely he had fully realized the substance of his mind, leaving nothing unilluminated; thus, when he shone his light upon the affairs of the world, no distance lay beyond its reach. Those people of Hexi saw only that, from ten thousand li away, he knew of affairs before they were undertaken and responded to developments just as they were about to emerge. They merely found this startling and astonishing. Who among them understood that it was rooted in this? Ah! Was this not why Guangwu revived the achievements of orderly government in the dynastic restoration, recovered the former possessions of Gao and Ren [?], and was called an enlightened ruler? Those in this world who seek out petty details, scrutinize the tips of autumn hairs, and illuminate fish in the depths, taking this for enlightenment, are merely…

語此哉則天地之大輝日月之光盈心體
之明窮物理之盡智周萬物之微明見萬

translation_en:
…merely the discernment of petty scrutiny, the wisdom of smug cleverness, and the selfishness of anticipating deceit. How could these suffice to speak of such understanding? As for the vast radiance of Heaven and Earth, the full brilliance of sun and moon, the illumination of the mind’s essential substance, the exhaustive comprehension of the principles of things, wisdom encompassing the subtleties of all things, and discernment reaching ten thousand li away—qualities that put Guangwu, a thousand and more years ago, to shame—these are manifest [?] in the sacred Son of Heaven of our own day.

We now observe the advent of spring in the chamber hung with red silk, and thereby verify the ordering of the seasons through the jade instruments [?]. The four…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
始循環而不已二氣迭運以無窮剝往復
來天地之心以見陰消陽長君子之道斯
亨萬物彙萌群生惟動茲盖伏遇
○○○○
聖本天成
敬循日緝
紹統緒而正位宸極五載於茲
主七鬯而毓德青宮十年之久
一德潛孚於上下
===
重光普照於華夷會千載之昌期際一陽之
嘉節循舊儀以納貢
受履迎祥法大禮以無為
臨朝拱默配天配地廣矣舜之為君如日如
雲大哉堯之為帝萬類霑
恩於罔律八荒仰
德於垂衣
奉歡慶於
兩宮載致長春之祝
punctuated: 始循環而不已，二氣迭運以無窮。剝往復來，天地之心以見；陰消陽長，君子之道斯亨。萬物彙萌，群生惟動。茲盖伏遇○○○○，聖本天成，敬循日緝。紹統緒而正位宸極，五載於茲；主七鬯而毓德青宮，十年之久。一德潛孚於上下，重光普照於華夷。會千載之昌期，際一陽之嘉節。循舊儀以納貢，受履迎祥；法大禮以無為，臨朝拱默。配天配地，廣矣舜之為君；如日如雲，大哉堯之為帝。萬類霑恩於罔律，八荒仰德於垂衣。奉歡慶於兩宮，載致長春之祝。
translation_en: …beginnings revolve without cease, and the two vital forces alternate endlessly. Decline departs and Return arrives, revealing the heart of Heaven and Earth; yin wanes and yang grows, and thus the way of the gentleman flourishes. All things sprout together, and every living being stirs. We now humbly encounter ○○○○: your sagely nature is Heaven-endowed, and your reverence is cultivated daily [?]. You have succeeded to the imperial line and taken your rightful place upon the throne, now for five years; you presided over the sacrificial ladle and fragrant wine [?] and nurtured your virtue in the crown prince’s palace for ten long years. Your single-minded virtue has silently won the trust of those above and below; your renewed radiance shines everywhere upon Chinese and foreign peoples alike. We meet an age of prosperity encountered once in a thousand years and arrive at the auspicious festival when the first yang returns. Following established ceremony, you receive tribute; accepting the increase of years, you welcome blessings. Taking the great rites as your model, you govern through nonaction; attending court, you sit silently with hands folded. Matching Heaven and Earth—how expansive was Shun’s rule as sovereign! Like the sun and the clouds—how great was Yao’s rule as emperor! All living things receive your boundless [?] grace; the eight distant regions look up to the virtue with which you rule, your robes hanging undisturbed. We offer joyous congratulations to the Two Palaces and present wishes for enduring spring.

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
錫燕惠於百辟用歌湛露之恩義馭轉於亨
衢萬方共仰王民席於化國九土咸宜臣
等樂生
盛世喜際佳辰式瞻亞歲之儀莫罄萬年之
慶効倉鶊以鳴卉愧赤日以傾葵伏願
任德不任刑用順陽生之義
保賢以保
國式昌道長之朝臣等無任瞻
天仰
===
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叅場
第一問
孫璋
同考試官教諭江　批〔敷荅〕
punctuated:
錫燕惠於百辟，用歌湛露之恩。義馭轉於亨衢，萬方共仰；王民席於化國，九土咸宜。臣等樂生盛世，喜際佳辰，式瞻亞歲之儀，莫罄萬年之慶。効倉鶊以鳴卉，愧赤日以傾葵。伏願任德不任刑，用順陽生之義；保賢以保國，式昌道長之朝。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
第叅場
第一問
孫璋
同考試官教諭江，批〔敷荅〕
translation_en:
…You bestow the favor of a banquet upon the assembled officials, who sing of your benevolence in “Abundant Dew.” The chariot of righteousness [?] turns along the road of prosperity, and all regions look up to it together; the king’s people dwell at ease in a realm transformed by moral influence, and all nine regions enjoy fitting conditions. We, your servants, rejoice to have been born in this flourishing age and are delighted to encounter this auspicious occasion. As we behold the ceremonies of the Lesser New Year, our congratulations on your reign of ten thousand years cannot be exhausted. We imitate the oriole singing at the flowering of plants, and humbly turn like sunflowers toward the radiant sun [?]. We reverently wish that you rely upon virtue rather than punishments, thereby following the principle of the birth of yang; and that you preserve the worthy so as to preserve the state, thereby bringing prosperity to a court in which the Way advances. Looking up to Heaven and revering Your Sagely Majesty, we, your servants, are overcome with fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulations for your hearing.
Third Session
First Question
Sun Zhang
Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: 〔An expansive response…〕

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
今上褒恤之仁詳覈無遺允宜錄出
朝
考試官學正濮　批〔歷叙我〕
太祖之創業元勲之佐命處考據得實條達無遺定群騏驥舍子其誰
考試官教授宋　批〔鋪張〕
聖朝褒錄勲舊之典詞義懇至其強識待問者與
對昔我
聖祖肇闢乾坤汛掃百年之屬
神功聖德蓋自古帝王之所未有一時佐命
元勲起際風雲芟薙四海之亂奇功偉略
亦自昔人臣之所罕見夫人臣有一世之
功宜享一世之報有百世之功宜享百世
之報今
===
國家有億萬世無疆之休則亦宜享億萬世
無疆之報者此所以有待於今日之
詔恩歟君臣感遇不偶然也漢高起豐沛而
蕭曹多豐沛之故人光武起南陽而李鄧
多南陽之近親唐太宗起晉陽而房杜多
punctuated:
今上褒恤之仁，詳覈無遺，允宜錄出朝。

考試官學正濮，批〔歷叙我〕太祖之創業、元勲之佐命處，考據得實，條達無遺。定群騏驥，舍子其誰？

考試官教授宋，批〔鋪張〕聖朝褒錄勲舊之典，詞義懇至，其強識待問者與？

對：昔我聖祖肇闢乾坤，汛掃百年之屬，神功聖德，蓋自古帝王之所未有。一時佐命元勲，起際風雲，芟薙四海之亂，奇功偉略，亦自昔人臣之所罕見。夫人臣有一世之功，宜享一世之報；有百世之功，宜享百世之報。今國家有億萬世無疆之休，則亦宜享億萬世無疆之報者，此所以有待於今日之詔恩歟？君臣感遇，不偶然也。漢高起豐沛，而蕭曹多豐沛之故人；光武起南陽，而李鄧多南陽之近親；唐太宗起晉陽，而房杜多
translation_en:
…the benevolence with which His Present Majesty honors and provides relief: the examination is thorough and leaves nothing out. This certainly merits selection for submission to the court [?].

Examiner Pu, Instructor, comments: 〔It recounts in sequence our〕 Taizu’s founding of the dynasty and the meritorious statesmen’s assistance in establishing his rule. Its evidence is sound, its exposition clear and comprehensive. Who but you could take the foremost place among this herd of thoroughbreds?

Examiner Song, Professor, comments: 〔It expounds〕 the august dynasty’s provisions for honoring and recognizing veteran men of merit. Its language and meaning are deeply earnest. Is this not someone of retentive memory, ready to answer questions?

Response: In former times our sagely founding ancestor first opened heaven and earth anew and swept away the remnants of a hundred years [?]. His divine achievements and sagely virtue were surely unmatched by any emperor or king of antiquity. The meritorious founders who assisted him in establishing his rule arose at that momentous juncture and cut away the disorder throughout the realm. Their extraordinary achievements and magnificent strategies, too, were rarely equaled by ministers of earlier times. A minister whose achievements benefit one generation should enjoy rewards for one generation; one whose achievements benefit a hundred generations should enjoy rewards for a hundred generations. Now that the dynasty enjoys boundless blessings for countless generations, they too should enjoy boundless rewards for countless generations. Is this why they have awaited the grace of today’s imperial edict?

The responsive encounter between ruler and ministers is no accident. Gaozu of Han rose in Feng and Pei, and Xiao He and Cao Shen were old acquaintances from Feng and Pei. Guangwu rose in Nanyang, and Li Tong and Deng Yu were close kinsmen from Nanyang [?]. Taizong of Tang rose in Jinyang, and Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui were mostly …

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
康府之舊我
太祖起淮右而元勳多淮右之人豈一州一邑
而有天下之傑哉蓋天生聖人以開萬世
太平之業則必生一世之豪傑以輔成其
功也世至胡元天地大變其亂也大其平
之也難是故漢高之勍敵項羽一人而已
光武太宗之所值赤眉王竇亦盜賊之靡
耳若元之季群雄並起江西則陳友亮姑
蘇則張士誠四川則明玉珎福建則陳有
定閩陝則李思齊張良弼而北都則元君
===
其餘紛紛籍籍爭相割據我
太祖自淮渡江遂都金陵鄱陽大戰而友亮殲
姑蘇肆圍而士誠縛水陸並進而明昇降
鐵騎長驅而元君遁其餘電驅霆擊氷消
瓦解天生神武固知
帝王之有真而一時佐命之功亦有可言者
國史所載非外人所得見也然愚嘗徧歷山
川考其碑誌覽當時戰鬭之所詢之父老
punctuated:
康府之舊。我太祖起淮右，而元勳多淮右之人，豈一州一邑而有天下之傑哉？蓋天生聖人以開萬世太平之業，則必生一世之豪傑以輔成其功也。世至胡元，天地大變，其亂也大，其平之也難。是故漢高之勍敵，項羽一人而已；光武、太宗之所值，赤眉、王、竇，亦盜賊之靡耳。若元之季，群雄並起：江西則陳友亮，姑蘇則張士誠，四川則明玉珎，福建則陳有定，閩陝則李思齊、張良弼，而北都則元君。其餘紛紛籍籍，爭相割據。我太祖自淮渡江，遂都金陵。鄱陽大戰而友亮殲，姑蘇肆圍而士誠縛，水陸並進而明昇降，鐵騎長驅而元君遁。其餘電驅霆擊，氷消瓦解。天生神武，固知帝王之有真，而一時佐命之功，亦有可言者。
國史所載，非外人所得見也。然愚嘗徧歷山川，考其碑誌，覽當時戰鬭之所，詢之父老，
translation_en:
…former retainers of the Prince of Kang’s establishment [?]. Our Taizu rose in Huaiyou, and many of his founding men of merit also came from Huaiyou. Could a single prefecture or county contain all the outstanding men of the realm? When Heaven brings forth a sage to establish an undertaking of enduring peace for ten thousand generations, it must also bring forth the heroes of an age to help him accomplish it. When the world reached the age of the barbarian Yuan, Heaven and Earth underwent a great upheaval. The disorder was immense, and restoring peace was difficult. Thus Gaozu of Han had only one formidable enemy, Xiang Yu. Those whom Guangwu and Taizong encountered—the Red Eyebrows, Wang, and Dou—were merely bands of robbers [?]. At the end of the Yuan, however, rival strongmen arose together: Chen Youliang in Jiangxi, Zhang Shicheng in Gusu, Ming Yuzhen in Sichuan, Chen Youding in Fujian, Li Siqi and Zhang Liangbi in Min and Shaanxi [?], and the Yuan ruler in the northern capital. Countless others competed to carve out territories for themselves. Our Taizu came from the Huai region, crossed the Yangzi, and established his capital at Jinling. In the great battle at Poyang, Youliang was annihilated; when Gusu was closely besieged, Shicheng was captured; when land and naval forces advanced together, Ming Sheng surrendered; and when the armored cavalry swept forward, the Yuan ruler fled. The remaining forces, assailed with the speed of lightning and the force of thunder, melted like ice and shattered like tiles. Heaven endowed him with divine martial prowess: assuredly we recognize in him a true sovereign. Yet the achievements of those who helped establish his mandate in that age also deserve to be recounted.
What is recorded in the dynastic history is inaccessible to outsiders. Nevertheless, I, in my humble capacity, have traveled widely through the mountains and rivers, examined inscriptions on stelae and funerary monuments, visited the battlefields of that time, and questioned local elders…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
亦略得其一二獨未知信否也敢以質於
執事盖聞配享元勲十二人首中山武寧
王徐達次則開平忠烈王常遇春岐陽武
靖王李文忠寧河順武王鄧愈東甌襄武
王湯和黔寧照靖王沐英五公則俞通海
張德勝胡大海趙德勝耿再成侯則桑世
傑皆開國元勲也削平南服蹙滁中原降
王縛將不可勝數其謀略似韓信其仁恕
似鄧禹其不伐似馮異其不殺似曹彬此
中山之功所以為我
朝元勲第一也采石先登康郎酣戰單騎衝
敵而河南歸疆全師轉戰而開平拓跡開
平之功世擬之尉遲敬德者也鏖兵富陽
連城來附揔兵應昌重寶獻捷遇敵則智
勇輻湊家居則經籍是耽此岐陽之功世
擬之祭遵者也滁陽歸義江西累功平蠻
蠻於溪峒追土蕃於崑崙雖更摧挫曾無
怨言此寧河之為將比之馬援者也守常
punctuated:
亦略得其一二，獨未知信否也，敢以質於執事。盖聞配享元勲十二人，首中山武寧王徐達，次則開平忠烈王常遇春、岐陽武靖王李文忠、寧河順武王鄧愈、東甌襄武王湯和、黔寧照靖王沐英。五公則俞通海、張德勝、胡大海、趙德勝、耿再成，侯則桑世傑，皆開國元勲也。
削平南服，蹙滁中原，降王縛將，不可勝數。其謀略似韓信，其仁恕似鄧禹，其不伐似馮異，其不殺似曹彬，此中山之功所以為我朝元勲第一也。
采石先登，康郎酣戰，單騎衝敵而河南歸疆，全師轉戰而開平拓跡。開平之功，世擬之尉遲敬德者也。
鏖兵富陽，連城來附；揔兵應昌，重寶獻捷。遇敵則智勇輻湊，家居則經籍是耽。此岐陽之功，世擬之祭遵者也。
滁陽歸義，江西累功，平蠻蠻於溪峒，追土蕃於崑崙，雖更摧挫，曾無怨言。此寧河之為將，比之馬援者也。
守常
translation_en:
…I have also learned a little of these matters, but do not yet know whether it is reliable, and venture to submit it to you for verification. I have heard that twelve founding men of outstanding merit were accorded accompanying sacrifices in the imperial ancestral temple. Foremost was Xu Da, Prince Wuning of Zhongshan; next were Chang Yuchun, Prince Zhonglie of Kaiping; Li Wenzhong, Prince Wujing of Qiyang; Deng Yu, Prince Shunwu of Ninghe; Tang He, Prince Xiangwu of Dong’ou; and Mu Ying, Prince Zhaojing of Qianning. The five dukes were Yu Tonghai, Zhang Desheng, Hu Dahai, Zhao Desheng, and Geng Zaicheng; the marquis was Sang Shijie. All were outstanding contributors to the dynasty’s founding.
He pacified the southern territories and pressed the enemy in the Central Plain [?], bringing kings to submission and capturing commanders beyond counting. His strategic skill resembled Han Xin’s; his humanity and forbearance, Deng Yu’s; his refusal to boast of his achievements, Feng Yi’s; and his restraint from killing, Cao Bin’s. Such were Zhongshan’s achievements, which made him foremost among our dynasty’s founding men of merit.
He was first to scale the defenses at Caishi and fought fiercely at Kanglang. Charging the enemy single-handed on horseback, he brought Henan within the realm; leading his entire army through successive battles, he extended its reach to Kaiping. For these achievements, the Prince of Kaiping is compared by contemporaries to Yuchi Jingde.
He fought fiercely at Fuyang, and cities submitted in succession; he commanded troops at Yingchang and presented precious treasures as tokens of victory. Facing the enemy, he combined wisdom and courage; at home, he immersed himself in the classics and other books. For these achievements, the Prince of Qiyang is compared by contemporaries to Ji Zun.
He pledged allegiance to the righteous cause at Chuyang and repeatedly earned merit in Jiangxi. He subdued the non-Han peoples [?] of the mountain streams and caves and pursued the Tibetans to Kunlun. Though he suffered setbacks, he never voiced resentment. Such was the Prince of Ninghe’s conduct as a general, for which he is compared to Ma Yuan.
Defending Chang…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
州而士誠不敢西向持尺書乞爾相率
來降略定閩中築城海上結髮相從獨全
終始此襄武之功比之曹參者也威振西
蕃愛存南詔既歿而父老立祠擬身虹縣
作鎮金華既歿而忠魂助陣則沐之忠愛
胡之忠烈見於陰騭書矣其餘或預建義
之功或著死難之鄧而不預配享者則有
誠意伯劉基帷幄秘謨幾先獨炳
上之呼之為子房者也韓國公李善長豐沛
===
勲舊輯和將士世擬之蕭何者也平蜀之
師以傳有德之功為最鄱陽之戰以廖永
忠之勇為奇於乎鐵券金書山河帶礪雲
臺凌煙英姿颯爽千載之下猶想風烈漢
唐功臣或以酎金失侯或以細故除國蕭
何之後至于絕祀陳平之後迄不得紹封
房杜子孫覆亡殆盡魏徵故第質錢於人
汾陽之宅為寺馬燧之第為園此古今之
所慨也今
punctuated: 州，而士誠不敢西向；持尺書，乞爾相率來降；略定閩中，築城海上。結髮相從，獨全終始。此襄武之功，比之曹參者也。威振西蕃，愛存南詔，既歿而父老立祠；擬身虹縣，作鎮金華，既歿而忠魂助陣。則沐之忠愛、胡之忠烈，見於《陰騭書》矣。其餘或預建義之功，或著死難之鄧，而不預配享者，則有誠意伯劉基，帷幄秘謨，幾先獨炳，上之呼之為子房者也；韓國公李善長，豐沛勲舊，輯和將士，世擬之蕭何者也。平蜀之師，以傳有德之功為最；鄱陽之戰，以廖永忠之勇為奇。於乎！鐵券金書，山河帶礪，雲臺凌煙，英姿颯爽，千載之下，猶想風烈。漢唐功臣，或以酎金失侯，或以細故除國。蕭何之後至于絕祀，陳平之後迄不得紹封，房杜子孫覆亡殆盡，魏徵故第質錢於人，汾陽之宅為寺，馬燧之第為園。此古今之所慨也。今
translation_en:
…[Chang]zhou, so that Shicheng dared not advance westward; bearing a short letter, he induced Qier [?] and the others to submit together. He subdued central Fujian and built fortifications on the coast. Having followed the ruler since youth, he alone preserved that bond from beginning to end. Such were the achievements of Xiangwu, who may be compared to Cao Can. One spread his military prestige through the western Tibetan regions and left a legacy of benevolence in Nanzhao; after his death, the elders erected a shrine. Another offered his service [?] in Hong County and commanded the garrison at Jinhua; after his death, his loyal spirit assisted in battle. Thus Mu’s loyalty and benevolence, and Hu’s loyalty and valor, are recorded in the Book of Hidden Recompense (Yinzhi shu). Among the others who contributed to the righteous uprising or distinguished themselves by dying in adversity [?], yet were not included in the accompanying sacrifices, was Liu Ji, Earl of Chengyi. Devising confidential strategies within the command tent, he alone perceived the first signs of events with clarity; the emperor called him Zifang. There was also Li Shanchang, Duke of Han, a veteran founding servant like those from Feng and Pei, who maintained harmony among officers and soldiers; people compared him to Xiao He. In the campaign to pacify Shu, Fu Youde’s achievements were foremost [the transcription gives 傳 for Fu]; in the battle of Poyang, Liao Yongzhong’s valor was extraordinary.

Ah! Iron patents inscribed in gold pledged enduring privilege until the rivers became narrow as belts and the mountains small as whetstones. Like the portraits in the Cloud Terrace and Lingyan Pavilion, their heroic figures stand spirited and imposing; even a thousand years later, one can still envision their noble bearing. Among the meritorious servants of the Han and Tang, some lost their marquisates over the gold contributions for the ancestral libations, while others had their fiefs abolished for trifling causes. Xiao He’s descendants eventually had no one left to maintain their ancestral sacrifices; Chen Ping’s descendants never succeeded in inheriting his enfeoffment. The descendants of Fang and Du were almost entirely destroyed. Wei Zheng’s former residence was mortgaged to others; the residence of the Prince of Fenyang became a Buddhist monastery, and Ma Sui’s mansion became a garden. These are matters lamented throughout the ages. Now…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖上念功錄舊詔恤其後四海歸心書曰茲予
大享於先王爾祖其從與享之詩曰凡周
之士不顯亦世豈三代亦以為盛爭猶恐
議者不思大義恩不下究使
聖朝之美鬱而不宣杜鄴有言雖難盡繼宜從
尤功最以此聞於廟堂之上至則為歌頌
着呂化光之贊柳宗元之雅鏗鍧炳燿以
彰
聖朝之盛則有玉堂燕許之筆非愚生所敢聞
===
也
第二問
張棨
同考試官訓導翁　批　諭教
元良闡時政切務卅篇條對洋洋且以
正心正官為要深得謹始大意可嘉可嘉
考試官學正濮　批　酌古準今指陳切當儼然而歎乎
上未必不為早諭教之一助
考試官教授宋　批　有考據有定見未而行之將有裨益
punctuated:
聖上念功錄舊，詔恤其後，四海歸心。《書》曰：「茲予大享於先王，爾祖其從與享之。」《詩》曰：「凡周之士，不顯亦世。」豈三代亦以為盛爭？猶恐議者不思大義，恩不下究，使聖朝之美鬱而不宣。杜鄴有言：「雖難盡繼，宜從尤功最。」以此聞於廟堂之上。至則為歌頌，着呂化光之贊、柳宗元之雅，鏗鍧炳燿，以彰聖朝之盛，則有玉堂燕許之筆，非愚生所敢聞也。

第二問
張棨

同考試官訓導翁批：諭教元良，闡時政切務，卅篇條對洋洋，且以正心正官為要，深得謹始大意。可嘉，可嘉！

考試官學正濮批：酌古準今，指陳切當，儼然而歎乎上，未必不為早諭教之一助。

考試官教授宋批：有考據，有定見，未而行之，將有裨益
translation_en:
…His Majesty remembers meritorious service and honors old servants, issuing an edict to provide for their descendants; all within the four seas give him their allegiance. The Book of Documents says: “Now I make a great offering to the former kings; your ancestors shall accompany them and share in it.” The Book of Odes says: “All the gentlemen of Zhou—are they not illustrious through the generations?” Could even the Three Dynasties have considered this a flourishing achievement [?]? Yet I fear that those who deliberate on this matter will fail to consider the greater moral obligation, that imperial grace will not reach those below, and that the excellence of our sage dynasty will remain concealed and unproclaimed. Du Ye said: “Although it is difficult to continue all hereditary successions, one should begin with those whose achievements were most outstanding.” Let this be brought before the court. As for composing songs of praise [?], writing encomia like those of Lü Huaguang and grand odes like those of Liu Zongyuan, resonant and brilliant, to display the splendor of our sage dynasty: there are pens in the Hanlin Academy comparable to those of the Dukes of Yan and Xu. This is something in which this foolish student would not dare claim a part.

Second Question
Zhang Qi

Comment by Associate Examiner Weng, Assistant Instructor: In discussing the instruction of the heir apparent, he expounds the pressing concerns of current government. The thirty essays provide ample, point-by-point responses [?]. Moreover, he takes rectifying the mind and rectifying officials as essential, thoroughly grasping the larger significance of exercising care at the outset. Commendable, commendable!

Comment by Examiner Pu, Instructor: He weighs antiquity against the present, and his observations are pertinent and fitting. With solemn bearing, he voices a lament before the throne [?]; this may well help promote the early instruction of the heir apparent.

Comment by Examiner Song, Instructor: He offers supporting evidence and firm judgments. If put into practice [?], this will prove beneficial …

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖心者得士如此足以驗人文之盛安得不載歌棫樸之章為
聖天子得人賀乎
天下之事有輕重聖人自其重者而行之
有緩急聖人自其急者而圖之何謂重國
本是也國本立而天下之志定事固有重
於此者乎何謂急早諭教是也諭教早而
儲君之德成事固有急於此者乎天祐
國家
===
元良篤降三靈慶社稷之無疆四海戴吾君
之有子潤加火海光耀前星天下之大本
定矣而今日所最急者請得言之人之言
曰時方幼冲學固未須講也愚以為不然
今凡人之家愛其子子之幼也擇母以保
之少長擇師以教之而況乎神器之所屬
天命之所歸宗社係以為安危生民係以
為休戚者乎古者太子廼生固舉以禮使
士負之見乎南郊自為赤子而教已行矣
自其能言而言有教自其能行而行有教
punctuated:
聖心者。得士如此，足以驗人文之盛，安得不載歌《棫樸》之章，為聖天子得人賀乎？

天下之事有輕重，聖人自其重者而行之；有緩急，聖人自其急者而圖之。何謂重？國本是也。國本立而天下之志定，事固有重於此者乎？何謂急？早諭教是也。諭教早而儲君之德成，事固有急於此者乎？天祐國家，元良篤降，三靈慶社稷之無疆，四海戴吾君之有子。潤加火海，光耀前星，天下之大本定矣。而今日所最急者，請得言之。人之言曰：「時方幼冲，學固未須講也。」愚以為不然。今凡人之家愛其子，子之幼也，擇母以保之；少長，擇師以教之。而況乎神器之所屬、天命之所歸、宗社係以為安危、生民係以為休戚者乎？古者太子廼生，固舉以禮，使士負之，見乎南郊，自為赤子而教已行矣。自其能言而言有教，自其能行而行有教。
translation_en:
…the imperial mind. Obtaining men of such talent is sufficient proof of the flourishing of literary culture. How could one refrain from singing the ode “Luxuriant Oaks” (Yupu) to congratulate the sagely Son of Heaven on obtaining worthy men?

Among the affairs of the world, some are less important and others more important: the sage acts first upon the more important. Some can wait and others are urgent: the sage attends first to the urgent. What is important? The foundation of the state. Once that foundation is established, the hearts of all under Heaven are settled. Can any matter be more important than this? What is urgent? Instructing and educating the heir early. Through early instruction, the crown prince’s virtue is brought to completion. Can any matter be more urgent than this?

Heaven has blessed the state, and a worthy heir has graciously been bestowed. The three divine powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—celebrate the boundless endurance of the altars of soil and grain, while all within the four seas rejoice that our sovereign has a son. Beneficence reaches the fiery sea [?], and radiance shines upon the Foremost Star, the celestial emblem of the heir apparent. The great foundation of all under Heaven is now secure. Yet permit me to speak of what is most urgent today.

Some say: “He is still very young; there is surely no need yet to discuss his schooling.” In my humble opinion, this is mistaken. Ordinary families today love their sons: in infancy they choose a nurse to care for them, and when they are a little older they choose a teacher to instruct them. How much more must this apply to the one to whom the sacred vessel of sovereignty is entrusted, upon whom Heaven’s Mandate devolves, upon whom the security or peril of the ancestral temples and state altars depends, and upon whom the well-being or suffering of the people depends?

In antiquity, immediately after a crown prince was born, he was lifted up according to ritual, and a serviceman was made to carry him for presentation at the southern suburban altar. His education thus began while he was still an infant. From the time he could speak, his speech was instructed; from the time he could walk, his conduct was instructed…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
成王之爲太子也置三師以職輔導又置
三少與之游處抗法則於伯禽游戲則於
唐叔所聞者必正言所見者必正事侍御
僕從皆士人也漢唐以降固已踈矣漢猶
詔郡國歲貢賢者以給宿衛授論語則於
張禹授尚書則於桓榮所用之人雖有愧
於古然當時猶得舉其職也唐制宮寮先
儒嘗稱其善詹事視中書省也贊善視諫
議大夫也劉洎馬周之徒遞日往東宮談
===
論所言雖有愧於古然猶得效其言也降
至近世堂陛尊嚴而上下之情踈禮節繁
多而君臣之義闕教者止於供職學者止
於備禮循行數墨立觧數語人情之邪正
不暇辨也民生之疾苦不暇知也義理之
淺深不暇問也古今之理亂不暇語也寒
暑間數月而見見不交一語而退退而與
之游者果何人歟不得而知也所行者果
何事歟不得而問也如是則雖有耆儒宿
punctuated:
成王之爲太子也，置三師以職輔導，又置三少與之游處。抗法則於伯禽，游戲則於唐叔。所聞者必正言，所見者必正事，侍御僕從皆士人也。漢唐以降，固已踈矣。漢猶詔郡國歲貢賢者，以給宿衛；授論語則於張禹，授尚書則於桓榮。所用之人雖有愧於古，然當時猶得舉其職也。唐制宮寮，先儒嘗稱其善：詹事視中書省也，贊善視諫議大夫也。劉洎、馬周之徒遞日往東宮談論，所言雖有愧於古，然猶得效其言也。

降至近世，堂陛尊嚴而上下之情踈，禮節繁多而君臣之義闕。教者止於供職，學者止於備禮。循行數墨，立觧數語；人情之邪正不暇辨也，民生之疾苦不暇知也，義理之淺深不暇問也，古今之理亂不暇語也。寒暑間數月而見，見不交一語而退。退而與之游者，果何人歟？不得而知也。所行者，果何事歟？不得而問也。如是，則雖有耆儒宿
translation_en:
When King Cheng was heir apparent, the Three Preceptors were appointed to take charge of assisting and guiding him, and the Three Junior Preceptors were also appointed to keep him company. In upholding proper standards he took Boqin as his model, and in play he took Tang Shu as his model. Whatever he heard was necessarily correct speech; whatever he saw was necessarily correct conduct. His attendants and servants were all men of learning. From the Han and Tang onward, these arrangements had admittedly grown lax. Yet the Han still ordered the commanderies and kingdoms to recommend worthy men annually to serve in the palace guard. Instruction in the Analects was entrusted to Zhang Yu, and instruction in the Book of Documents to Huan Rong. Although those employed fell short of the men of antiquity, they could still discharge their duties in their own time. Earlier Confucian scholars praised the excellence of the Tang system of Eastern Palace officials: the Supervisor of the Household corresponded to the Secretariat, and the Advisers to the Grand Masters of Remonstrance. Men such as Liu Ji and Ma Zhou went on alternate days to the Eastern Palace for discussion. Although what they said fell short of antiquity, their words could still have an effect.

Coming down to recent times, the imposing dignity of the court has left ruler and subjects distant in feeling, while the proliferation of ceremonial formalities has left the obligations between sovereign and minister unfulfilled. Teachers do no more than perform their official duties, and learners do no more than observe the prescribed courtesies. They follow the lines and count the written characters, producing explanations of a few phrases. There is no time to distinguish the depravity or rectitude of human dispositions, no time to learn of the people's suffering, no time to inquire into the depths of moral principles, and no time to discuss order and disorder in past and present. Through winter and summer, they meet only at intervals of several months; when they meet, they withdraw without exchanging a single word. After they withdraw, who are the people who keep the prince company? They cannot know. What does he actually do? They cannot inquire. Under such circumstances, even if there are venerable Confucian scholars and seasoned …

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
然亦何得於心而何裨於治乎此後世之
通弊也若其教之之法則文王世子之篇
賈誼治安之疏言之備矣術數非所當用
則固非所當學也篇翰非所當嗜亦非所
當廢也唐之文皇宋之太宗我朝
太祖
宣宗奎章睿藻流布中外海內仰星日之光華
後世睹雲霞之煥爛夫豈害於道乎但不
可篤好乎此耳如生之愚謂當妙選才賢
===
勿拘以地宏開講幄勿限以時更番直日
日侍宴閒講讀既罷從容燕語閭閻之疾
苦古今之理亂聞則游意篇翰亦勿拘焉
賈誼曰三代之所以長久者以其輔翼太
子有此具也茲非當今之所最急者乎
第三問
張憲
同考試官學正麗　批〔正道難行異端易售自古爲然此作據理答之而辭氣抑揚辨論反復真策手也〕
punctuated:
然亦何得於心，而何裨於治乎？此後世之通弊也。若其教之之法，則《文王世子》之篇、賈誼《治安》之疏言之備矣。術數非所當用，則固非所當學也；篇翰非所當嗜，亦非所當廢也。唐之文皇、宋之太宗、我朝太祖、宣宗，奎章睿藻流布中外，海內仰星日之光華，後世睹雲霞之煥爛，夫豈害於道乎？但不可篤好乎此耳。如生之愚，謂當妙選才賢，勿拘以地；宏開講幄，勿限以時；更番直日，日侍宴閒。講讀既罷，從容燕語，閭閻之疾苦、古今之理亂。聞則游意篇翰，亦勿拘焉。賈誼曰：「三代之所以長久者，以其輔翼太子有此具也。」茲非當今之所最急者乎？

第三問
張憲
同考試官學正麗　批〔正道難行，異端易售，自古爲然。此作據理答之，而辭氣抑揚，辨論反復，真策手也。〕
translation_en:
…yet what could he gain inwardly, and what benefit could he bring to government? This is a common failing of later ages. As for the methods of educating him, these are fully explained in the chapter “King Wen as Heir Apparent” and Jia Yi’s Memorial on Good Order and Security. Techniques of calculation and divination are inappropriate to employ and thus certainly inappropriate to study. Literary composition should not become an absorbing passion, but neither should it be abandoned. Emperor Wen of the Tang, Taizong of the Song, and Taizu and Xuanzong of our own dynasty circulated their imperial writings within and beyond the realm. All within the seas looked up to their radiance as to the stars and sun; later generations beheld their splendor as that of luminous clouds. How could these writings have harmed the Way? One must simply avoid becoming excessively devoted to them.

In this humble student’s opinion, talented and worthy men should be selected with the utmost care, without restrictions based on locality. Instruction in the lecture chamber should be generously provided, without restrictions on its timing. Instructors should take turns on daily duty and attend him each day during his leisure. Once lectures and readings have ended, they should converse informally and at ease about the hardships of ordinary people and the causes of order and disorder, past and present. After hearing these matters, he may also turn his attention to literary composition without undue restriction [?]. Jia Yi said: “The Three Dynasties endured so long because they possessed this full provision for assisting and guiding the heir apparent.” Is this not among the most urgent matters of the present day?

Third Policy Question
Zhang Xian
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔The orthodox Way is difficult to put into practice, while heterodox teachings readily find acceptance: this has been so since antiquity. This essay answers on the basis of principle; its language and tone rise and fall, and its arguments examine the issues repeatedly. Here is a true master of the policy essay.〕

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭劉　批〔正道未必無效異端未必可行此篇〕
〔復辯論卒歸於正必有識之士也允宜高薦〕
考試官學正濮　批〔初二場連閱子卷已知爲不凡士矣及〕
〔觀此策敷發正道異端卓有斷制益知真爲瑚璉貢子〕
考試官教授宋　批〔論正道異端以笑難易斷之卓有定識〕
天下無道外之事其存乎人也有淺深其
行於世也有難易淺深存乎人者也難易
存乎天者也事有不幸而當邪正勍似之
〔天府必爲清廟之用無疑矣健羨健羨〕
===
問天人雜糅之際此事功所以參差不齊
道之所以難行世之所以難治人之所以
難論也嗟夫天下無易事而值事機之會
者見其易天下無難事而值事機之去者
見其難道固不以是加損也子房之學優
爲帝師當其學禮倉海君固未知其所講
者何事而愽浪狙擊蓋得春秋復仇之義
赤松避㯲亦似大易知幾之神追項籍蓋
推亡固存之道封韓信蓋有忍乃濟之謀
punctuated:
同考試官教諭劉，批〔正道未必無效，異端未必可行，此篇〕〔復辯論，卒歸於正，必有識之士也，允宜高薦。〕
考試官學正濮，批〔初二場連閱子卷，已知爲不凡士矣，及〕〔觀此策，敷發正道異端，卓有斷制，益知真爲瑚璉貢子。〕
考試官教授宋，批〔論正道異端，以笑難易斷之，卓有定識。〕
天下無道外之事，其存乎人也有淺深，其行於世也有難易。淺深存乎人者也，難易存乎天者也。事有不幸而當邪正勍似之〔天府，必爲清廟之用無疑矣。健羨健羨！〕問，天人雜糅之際，此事功所以參差不齊，道之所以難行，世之所以難治，人之所以難論也。嗟夫！天下無易事，而值事機之會者見其易；天下無難事，而值事機之去者見其難。道固不以是加損也。子房之學，優爲帝師。當其學禮倉海君，固未知其所講者何事，而愽浪狙擊，蓋得《春秋》復仇之義；赤松避㯲，亦似《大易》知幾之神；追項籍，蓋推亡固存之道；封韓信，蓋有忍乃濟之謀。
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The correct Way is not necessarily ineffective, nor are heterodox teachings necessarily practicable. This essay〕〔argues the matter further and ultimately returns to what is correct. Its author must be a man of discernment and truly deserves a high recommendation.〕
Examiner Pu, a School Instructor, comments: 〔Having read your scripts in succession for the first two sessions, I already knew you to be an exceptional scholar. When〕〔I examined this policy essay, with its exposition of the correct Way and heterodox teachings and its remarkably decisive judgments, I became still more certain that you are truly a tribute scholar of the calibre of the hu and lian sacrificial vessels [?].〕
Examiner Song, a Professor, comments: 〔In discussing the correct Way and heterodox teachings, he judges their difficulty and ease “with laughter” [?], displaying remarkably firm discernment.〕
Nothing under Heaven lies outside the Way. In people, its presence may be shallow or deep; in the world, its implementation may be difficult or easy. Shallowness and depth depend on people; difficulty and ease depend on Heaven. When affairs unfortunately fall at a juncture where the deviant and the correct are closely alike [?]—〔in the celestial treasury [?]; there is no doubt that you will be employed in the pure ancestral temple. How greatly I admire you, how greatly I admire you!〕—and where Heaven and human action intermingle, this is why achievements are uneven, why the Way is difficult to put into practice, why the world is difficult to govern, and why people are difficult to judge. Alas! Nothing under Heaven is easy, yet those who encounter a convergence of opportunities find it easy. Nothing under Heaven is difficult, yet those who encounter the passing of opportunities find it difficult. The Way itself is neither increased nor diminished by this.
Zifang’s learning amply qualified him to be an emperor’s teacher. When he studied ritual with Lord Canghai [?], we do not know precisely what he discussed. Yet his ambush at Bolang surely grasped the principle of vengeance in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His withdrawal with Chisong to escape prohibitions [?] likewise resembled the wondrous discernment of incipient changes described in the Great Book of Changes. His pursuit of Xiang Ji embodied the way of overthrowing those destined to perish and securing those destined to endure; his enfeoffment of Han Xin embodied the strategy of achieving success through forbearance.…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
從容帷幄借箸運籌此豈圯下老人之所
教哉孔明之才自宜王佐當其游學潁川
獨觀大略固已異於曲士之所為隆中三
顧蓋庶乎渭濱莘野之聘出師二表又庶
乎伊訓說命之文屬精治蜀人有至死而
不怨雜耕渭濱敵有至死而不敢追而惓
惓漢賊反覆天人此豈管樂之所及哉貫
生於漢道初成之際經營講畫不遺餘慮
正朔之改制度之定達之仁義禮樂此豈
===
講於申韓者也申韓之書直發其經世之
志耳魏徵於太宗求治如不及之時孜孜
論諫王伯之別忠良之辨雖未及乎禮樂
之任此豈得之從横者也從横之學直發
其遇合之機耳若夫王荆公其經學非不
深也其行義非不整也其言法先王之意
以治天下非不正也而擯斥老成援引凶
邪此豈經學之所有哉其初起於執拗之
私其終成於紹述之禍前數子以豪傑之
punctuated:
從容帷幄，借箸運籌，此豈圯下老人之所教哉？孔明之才，自宜王佐。當其游學潁川，獨觀大略，固已異於曲士之所為。隆中三顧，蓋庶乎渭濱莘野之聘；出師二表，又庶乎伊訓說命之文。屬精治蜀，人有至死而不怨；雜耕渭濱，敵有至死而不敢追。而惓惓漢賊，反覆天人，此豈管樂之所及哉？貫生於漢道初成之際，經營講畫，不遺餘慮。正朔之改，制度之定，達之仁義禮樂，此豈講於申韓者也？申韓之書，直發其經世之志耳。
魏徵於太宗求治如不及之時，孜孜論諫，王伯之別，忠良之辨，雖未及乎禮樂之任，此豈得之從横者也？從横之學，直發其遇合之機耳。
若夫王荆公，其經學非不深也，其行義非不整也，其言法先王之意以治天下非不正也。而擯斥老成，援引凶邪，此豈經學之所有哉？其初起於執拗之私，其終成於紹述之禍。前數子以豪傑之
translation_en:
…At ease within the command tent, he borrowed chopsticks to lay out his strategy: could this have been what the old man at the bridge taught him? Kongming’s abilities naturally fitted him to assist a true king. While studying in Yingchuan, he alone attended to the broad essentials, already distinguishing himself from narrow-minded scholars. The three visits to Longzhong approached the invitations extended to worthy men on the banks of the Wei and in the fields of Shen. His two memorials on dispatching the army likewise approached the writings “Instructions of Yi” and “Charge to Yue.” He devoted his energies to governing Shu, and its people bore him no resentment even unto death. He interspersed his soldiers with farmers to cultivate land beside the Wei, and his enemies did not dare pursue him even at his death [?]. His abiding concern with the distinction between the Han and its usurpers, and his repeated reflections on Heaven and human affairs—could Guan Zhong and Yue Yi have equaled these? Guan Sheng [?; probably Jia Sheng, or Jia Yi] lived when the Han order was first taking shape. In planning and deliberation, he left nothing unconsidered. Reforming the calendar, establishing institutions, and extending these to benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music—could these have been teachings learned from Shen Buhai and Han Fei? Their books merely awakened his ambition to bring order to the world.
When Taizong sought good government as though he could never attain it, Wei Zheng tirelessly offered counsel and remonstrance concerning the distinction between kingly and hegemonic rule and the discernment of loyal and worthy men. Although he did not reach the point of undertaking responsibility for ritual and music, could he have acquired these insights from the strategists of diplomatic alliances? Their learning merely opened the opportunity for him to encounter a receptive ruler.
As for Wang, Duke of Jing, his learning in the Classics was certainly profound; his conduct in accordance with righteousness was certainly disciplined; and his proposal to govern the realm by emulating the intentions of the former kings was certainly correct. Yet he cast aside mature and experienced men and advanced the wicked and depraved. Could this have belonged to the learning of the Classics? It began in his selfish obstinacy and ended in the calamity of continuing his policies. The several men discussed earlier, with their outstanding…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
才其或未純者功利之累王荊公以功利
之說其飾也乃以三代之文今見數子之
功業則指為異端之可用見荊公之相業
則指為吾道之難行其可乎若乃程朱則
有可言者蓋二公平日所講者孔孟之微
言自諸子以下有不為所志者堯舜之大
道自兩漢以下有不道程子之在經筵以
先王之道為必可行務欲得於涵養薰陶
之際而不徒取於頰舌辯論之間朱子之
===
再召入也正心誠意之學不肯少貶且欲
存養於虛明應物之際以審察夫是非得
失之幾此皆可以格君心之非所謂還至
而立有效非無用之空言也而黨人之碑
僞學之禁道之難行自古而然其所以至
此者天也非人也夫諸賢之於道愚固未
暇議其所至之淺深獨以子房魏徵值其
易伊川晦翁值其難賈生值易而難孔明
值難而易而王荊公者固未可以並論也
punctuated: 才，其或未純者，功利之累。王荊公以功利之說，其飾也，乃以三代之文。今見數子之功業，則指為異端之可用；見荊公之相業，則指為吾道之難行，其可乎？若乃程朱，則有可言者。蓋二公平日所講者，孔孟之微言，自諸子以下有不為；所志者，堯舜之大道，自兩漢以下有不道。程子之在經筵，以先王之道為必可行，務欲得於涵養薰陶之際，而不徒取於頰舌辯論之間。朱子之再召入也，正心誠意之學不肯少貶，且欲存養於虛明應物之際，以審察夫是非得失之幾。此皆可以格君心之非，所謂還至而立有效，非無用之空言也。而黨人之碑、僞學之禁，道之難行，自古而然。其所以至此者，天也，非人也。夫諸賢之於道，愚固未暇議其所至之淺深，獨以子房、魏徵值其易，伊川、晦翁值其難，賈生值易而難，孔明值難而易，而王荊公者，固未可以並論也。
translation_en:
…talent; where these men fell short of complete purity, it was because they were encumbered by the pursuit of achievement and advantage. Wang Jinggong espoused doctrines of achievement and advantage, adorning them with the cultural forms of the Three Dynasties. Now, to see these men's accomplishments and declare that heterodox teachings can be useful, yet to see Jinggong's achievements as chief councillor and declare that our Way is difficult to put into practice—can this be acceptable?

As for Cheng and Zhu, there is something to be said. What these two masters expounded in their daily lives were the subtle teachings of Confucius and Mencius; among the teachings of the various masters and those after them, there were things they would not pursue. What they aspired to was the great Way of Yao and Shun; among the practices of the two Han dynasties and subsequent ages, there were things they would not discuss. While serving at the Classics Colloquium, Master Cheng held that the Way of the former kings could certainly be put into practice. He sought earnestly to achieve this through nurturing and gradual moral influence, rather than merely through eloquent debate. When Master Zhu was summoned back to court, he would not compromise in the slightest his teaching of rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere. He also sought to preserve and nurture the mind's openness and clarity as it responded to things, so as to discern the incipient distinctions between right and wrong, success and failure. All these methods could rectify what was wrong in the ruler's mind. This is what is meant by attaining the goal and immediately producing results [?]; these were no empty words without practical use.

Yet there were the stele listing factional men and the prohibition of ‘spurious learning.’ The difficulty of putting the Way into practice has been so since antiquity. That matters reached this point was due to Heaven, not to men. As for how deeply these worthy men attained the Way, I, in my ignorance, have not had leisure to discuss it. I would say only that Zifang and Wei Zheng encountered favorable circumstances, whereas Yichuan and Huiweng encountered difficulties; Master Jia encountered favorable circumstances that proved difficult, while Kongming encountered difficult circumstances that proved favorable. Wang Jinggong, however, certainly cannot be discussed on the same footing.

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
執事其以為何如
第四問
儀鳳禎
同考試官訓導喬　批　自東漢求爭言久任而不知久任
〔固自有要也此策得之〕
考試官學正濮　批　用人一策有考據有斷制非敷衍
〔問目者比其殫學待問者歟〕
考試官教授宋　批　識此意者可以相天下矣
善立法者必主於常善用法者不膠於常
===
必主於常故人各安其分而無覬覦之心
不膠於常故人得以慰其心而無怠惰之
意此昔之相天下者所以鼓舞一世之人
才而人樂為之用歟竊嘗思之今之天下
亦古之天下何古者人才之多而今世每
有乏才之歎歟豈天固不生才於今之世
歟無亦用之不得其道歟夫用之得其道
天下無不可用之人用之不得其道天下
無可用之人世之娖娖廉謹者抱守尺寸
punctuated:
執事其以為何如？

第四問
儀鳳禎

同考試官訓導喬，批：自東漢求爭言久任，而不知久任〔固自有要也，此策得之〕。
考試官學正濮，批：用人一策，有考據，有斷制，非敷衍〔問目者比，其殫學待問者歟〕。
考試官教授宋，批：識此意者，可以相天下矣。

善立法者必主於常，善用法者不膠於常。必主於常，故人各安其分，而無覬覦之心；不膠於常，故人得以慰其心，而無怠惰之意。此昔之相天下者所以鼓舞一世之人才，而人樂為之用歟？竊嘗思之：今之天下，亦古之天下，何古者人才之多，而今世每有乏才之歎歟？豈天固不生才於今之世歟？無亦用之不得其道歟？夫用之得其道，天下無不可用之人；用之不得其道，天下無可用之人。世之娖娖廉謹者，抱守尺寸
translation_en:
…What is your judgment on this, sir?

Fourth Policy Question
Yi Fengzhen 儀鳳禎

Associate Examiner Qiao, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Since the Eastern Han, [people have sought and contended?] in advocating long tenure, without understanding that long tenure 〔certainly has its own essential principles. This policy essay grasps them〕.”
Examiner Pu, Instructor, comments: “This policy essay on employing men offers both supporting evidence and decisive judgments. It cannot be compared with those that merely elaborate 〔the question’s wording. Is its author one who has devoted himself fully to learning, ready to be questioned〕?”
Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: “One who understands this principle could serve as chief minister of the realm.”

Those skilled in establishing regulations must take constancy as their guiding principle; those skilled in applying regulations do not cling rigidly to constancy. Because constancy must be their guiding principle, everyone rests content with his allotted position and harbors no ambitions to acquire what is not his. Because they do not cling rigidly to constancy, people find reassurance and entertain no inclination toward indolence. Was this how those who served as chief ministers of the realm in former times inspired the talented men of their age, so that people gladly served them?

I have ventured to reflect on this: the world today is also the world of antiquity. Why were talented men so numerous in antiquity, while today we repeatedly hear lamentations about their scarcity? Can it be that Heaven simply produces no talent in the present age? Might it instead be that we fail to employ people in the proper way? If people are employed in the proper way, there is no one in the realm who cannot be put to use; if they are employed improperly, there is no one in the realm who can be put to use. Those in the world who are scrupulously honest and cautious cling to narrow limits…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
而有賢愚同滯之譏其自許卓偉者多自
為好惡而有桃李私植之議無乃未識古
人立法用法之深意乎唐虞之世重黎世
掌天地夔契分掌禮樂而幽明之陟黜乃
在九載之後則唐虞亦久任也故鯀之治
水九載弗績而後罰一罰之則至殛死禹
之治水九州攸同而後賞一賞之則至宅
百揆其行久任有道矣下至西漢此意猶
存法令則湯禹文章則弘舒奉使則張騫
===
蘇武而倉氏庫氏至長子孫此西漢之久
任也故張釋之十年不調然調之則有一
歲至太中大夫者楊雄三世不徙然徙之
有自太守為宰相者其久任亦有法矣天
下見其委任之有常也故各安其分而不
敢望非其所當得見其超擢之不次也皆
奮起於事功而無委靡不振之患東漢以
降任人不常守宰數易疲於道路官知易
淌則懷遷民知易遷則苟且此牧民者之
punctuated: 而有賢愚同滯之譏。其自許卓偉者，多自為好惡，而有桃李私植之議，無乃未識古人立法用法之深意乎？唐虞之世，重黎世掌天地，夔契分掌禮樂，而幽明之陟黜乃在九載之後，則唐虞亦久任也。故鯀之治水，九載弗績而後罰，一罰之則至殛死；禹之治水，九州攸同而後賞，一賞之則至宅百揆。其行久任有道矣。下至西漢，此意猶存：法令則湯禹，文章則弘舒，奉使則張騫蘇武，而倉氏庫氏至長子孫，此西漢之久任也。故張釋之十年不調，然調之則有一歲至太中大夫者；楊雄三世不徙，然徙之有自太守為宰相者。其久任亦有法矣。天下見其委任之有常也，故各安其分，而不敢望非其所當得；見其超擢之不次也，皆奮起於事功，而無委靡不振之患。東漢以降，任人不常，守宰數易，疲於道路。官知易淌則懷遷，民知易遷則苟且。此牧民者之
translation_en:
…and thus incur the criticism that worthy and foolish alike are left to languish. Those who consider themselves outstanding often indulge their own likes and dislikes, provoking accusations that they privately cultivate protégés. Could it be that they have failed to understand the profound intentions of the ancients in establishing and applying rules?

In the age of Tang and Yu, Chong and Li held hereditary responsibility for heaven and earth, while Kui and Xie separately oversaw ritual and music. Yet promotion and dismissal according to whether officials were ineffectual or accomplished came only after nine years. Thus Tang and Yu also kept officials long in office. Gun was punished only after nine years of unsuccessful efforts to control the floods; once punishment came, it extended to execution. Yu was rewarded only after his flood-control efforts had brought the Nine Provinces into harmony; once rewarded, he was installed as chief minister. They had a proper way of implementing long tenure.

Even under the Western Han, this intention survived: Tang and Yu in laws and ordinances, Hong and Shu in literary composition, Zhang Qian and Su Wu on diplomatic missions, and the Cang and Ku families, whose responsibilities extended to their descendants [?]. Such was the Western Han practice of long tenure. Thus Zhang Shizhi went ten years without a change of appointment, yet when advancement came, he rose within a single year to Grand Master of Palace Leisure. Yang Xiong remained without a transfer through three reigns, yet when transfer came, there were those who advanced from governor to chief minister [?]. Their practice of long tenure, too, had its rules.

People throughout the realm saw the constancy of these appointments, so each remained content with his allotted position and dared not hope for what he ought not receive. Seeing that exceptional promotions could bypass the normal sequence, all exerted themselves to achieve results in office, without lapsing into listlessness and inertia. From the Eastern Han onward, appointments became inconstant. Governors and magistrates were frequently replaced, exhausting themselves on the roads. Officials, knowing that they could readily be transferred [?], thought of moving elsewhere; the people, knowing that officials could readily be transferred, merely muddled along. This was the condition of those who governed the people…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
不常也地形山川不及知軍情士伍不及
識此將兵者之不常也然使即行久任之
法則後來之人才又將何以處之壅塞之
憂淹滯之歎真有如執事所慮者愚以為
行此必有法也法者何慎擇之於始委任
之於中振發之於終慎擇之於始則不才
者無以容而無壅塞之憂委任之於中則
賢者得以行其志而無苟簡之弊振作之
於終則賢者得以慰其心而無淹滯之歎
===
奚會天下之才而分任之有心計者治財
有將略者治兵有政事者司民牧而為之
限或九年或六年其間有非常之績者則
不次而拔之其次焉則增秩奬勵而勿奪
其效又次焉雖不增秩秩滿而超遷之其
不才者亟去之使不得久其惡如是則得
之者自喜而奮起於功名不得者亦必爭
自洗磨以求知於上蓋所守者有常之法
所運者法外之意然二者必皆出於天下
punctuated:
不常也。地形山川不及知，軍情士伍不及識，此將兵者之不常也。然使即行久任之法，則後來之人才又將何以處之？壅塞之憂，淹滯之歎，真有如執事所慮者。愚以為行此必有法也。法者何？慎擇之於始，委任之於中，振發之於終。慎擇之於始，則不才者無以容，而無壅塞之憂；委任之於中，則賢者得以行其志，而無苟簡之弊；振作之於終，則賢者得以慰其心，而無淹滯之歎。

奚會天下之才而分任之：有心計者治財，有將略者治兵，有政事者司民牧。而為之限，或九年，或六年。其間有非常之績者，則不次而拔之；其次焉，則增秩奬勵，而勿奪其效；又次焉，雖不增秩，秩滿而超遷之。其不才者亟去之，使不得久其惡。如是，則得之者自喜而奮起於功名，不得者亦必爭自洗磨，以求知於上。蓋所守者有常之法，所運者法外之意。然二者必皆出於天下
translation_en:
…lack of continuity in office. They have no time to learn the terrain, mountains, and rivers, or to become acquainted with military circumstances and the ranks of their troops: this is the lack of continuity among military commanders. Yet if the system of long tenure were put into practice immediately, how would talented men who emerged later be accommodated? The worry that advancement would be blocked and the lament that men would languish in obscurity would indeed be just as you fear. In my humble opinion, there must be a method for implementing this. What is that method? Choose men carefully at the outset, entrust them with responsibility during their service, and spur them onward at its conclusion. If men are chosen carefully at the outset, the incompetent will have no place, and there will be no fear of blocked advancement. If men are entrusted with responsibility during their service, the worthy will be able to carry out their aspirations, without the fault of perfunctory administration. If they are spurred onward at its conclusion, the worthy will find their hearts satisfied, without lamenting that they languish in obscurity.

Bring together [?] the talented men of the realm and assign them separate responsibilities: let those skilled in calculation administer finances, those with strategic ability manage military affairs, and those versed in government oversee the people as their shepherds. Set terms for them, whether nine years or six. Those who achieve extraordinary results during that time should be promoted outside the regular sequence. Those in the next category should be encouraged with an increase in rank, without being deprived of the opportunity to bring their work to fruition. Those in the category below that, even if their rank is not increased, should receive exceptional promotion upon completing their terms. Remove the incompetent promptly, so that they cannot persist in their wrongdoing. In this way, those who obtain appointments will rejoice and strive for achievement and distinction; those who do not will likewise compete to reform and cultivate themselves, seeking recognition from their superiors. What is maintained is an established rule; what is exercised is judgment beyond the rule. Yet both must proceed from the realm’s…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
之公而后天下無異議愚以為有天下之
公執天下之法而又識法外之意然後可
以為宰相而任天下之賢不識執事以為
然乎
第五問
張夏
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔備邊之策上欲觀士子學識此策〕〔以兵馬財三者皆歸重於擇將確然有見真傑士也〕
考試官學正濮　批〔審擇邊將務在得人將得其人則無患〕
〔兵財馬不足矣軍政豈有不舉乎此策區處事宜適中表其經濟之論〕
考試官教授宋　批〔邊務之急在兵財馬三者此答善於〕
〔區處鑿鑿可行必有用之才也〕
===
事有自然之勢循其勢而置之得其道則
有餘逆其勢而置之不得其道則不足置
事如奕棋棋一也敗者不足勝者有餘敗
者据局凝思自以為無遺慮奕秋從旁為
易置之則勝矣勝者之奕敗者之棋也山
西控帶邊陲為今日北門之鎖鑰雲中第
punctuated:
之公，而后天下無異議。愚以為，有天下之公，執天下之法，而又識法外之意，然後可以為宰相，而任天下之賢。不識執事以為然乎？

第五問
張夏
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔備邊之策，上欲觀士子學識。此策〕〔以兵馬財三者皆歸重於擇將，確然有見，真傑士也。〕
考試官學正濮　批〔審擇邊將，務在得人。將得其人，則無患〕〔兵財馬不足矣。軍政豈有不舉乎？此策區處事宜適中，表其經濟之論。〕
考試官教授宋　批〔邊務之急，在兵財馬三者。此答善於〕〔區處，鑿鑿可行，必有用之才也。〕

事有自然之勢，循其勢而置之，得其道則有餘；逆其勢而置之，不得其道則不足。置事如奕棋，棋一也，敗者不足，勝者有餘。敗者据局凝思，自以為無遺慮，奕秋從旁為易置之，則勝矣。勝者之奕，敗者之棋也。山西控帶邊陲，為今日北門之鎖鑰。雲中第
translation_en:
…the impartiality of all under Heaven; only then will there be no dissent throughout the realm. In my humble view, only someone who possesses such impartiality, upholds the laws of the realm, and also understands the intent beyond those laws can serve as chief minister and appoint the realm’s worthy men. I wonder whether you, sir, consider this correct.

Fifth Question
Zhang Xia

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔Through this policy question on frontier defense, His Majesty wishes to assess the candidates’ learning and understanding. This essay〕〔makes the selection of generals the central consideration in all three matters—troops, horses, and funds. It displays firm insight: truly an outstanding scholar!〕

Comment by Examiner Pu, Assistant Instructor: 〔In carefully selecting frontier generals, the essential task is to obtain the right men. With the right men as generals, there need be no concern〕〔about insufficient troops, funds, or horses. How could military administration then fail to be carried out? This essay makes appropriate arrangements for the matters at hand, displaying the author’s arguments on statecraft.〕

Comment by Examiner Song, Instructor: 〔The urgent concerns of frontier affairs are these three: troops, funds, and horses. This answer excels in〕〔arranging matters; its proposals are sound and practicable. The author must possess talent that can be put to use.〕

Affairs have their natural tendencies. If one follows those tendencies in making arrangements and finds the proper method, resources will be ample; if one goes against them and fails to find the proper method, resources will be insufficient. Managing affairs is like playing weiqi. The game is the same, yet the loser has too little while the winner has more than enough. The loser sits at the board in deep thought, believing he has overlooked nothing; but if Yi Qiu, standing beside him, rearranges the pieces for him, victory follows. title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
一代州鴈門次之邊人所患者曰無兵也
無財也無馬也而愚以爲皆有之晋魏之
兵甞強於天下澤潞子弟亦甞雄於邊矣
至於今山河固無恙也昔也有中國之敵
今也有天下之助昔以之而有餘今以之
而不足此愚之所未觧也無亦曰措置之
不得其道乎今沿邊控弦鳴鏑帶甲百萬
兵固不不足也而邊臣有濟師之請朝使
之差所以蒐輯逃亡者甚嚴然亡
===
土著之兵以東南腴脆之人當西
北悍之虜水土不服險阻不諳廬舍不
定逃者未到而復亡追者愈嚴亡者愈甚
民間有搜捕之擾官府有稽考之煩而邊
陲未甞一賴其用愚以爲沿邊之人驍悍
鷙勇便於弓馬銳於戰闘召募而用之皆
爲精兵今人之所以憚爲兵者何也以尺
籍一定世世不移外有死亡之憂内有侵
剋之患今宜數外別爲尺籍壯勇是募優
punctuated: 一，代州鴈門次之。邊人所患者，曰無兵也，無財也，無馬也，而愚以爲皆有之。晋魏之兵甞強於天下，澤潞子弟亦甞雄於邊矣。至於今，山河固無恙也。昔也有中國之敵，今也有天下之助；昔以之而有餘，今以之而不足，此愚之所未觧也。無亦曰措置之不得其道乎？今沿邊控弦鳴鏑，帶甲百萬，兵固不不足也，而邊臣有濟師之請。朝使之差，所以蒐輯逃亡者甚嚴。然亡土著之兵，以東南腴脆之人當西北悍之虜，水土不服，險阻不諳，廬舍不定，逃者未到而復亡，追者愈嚴，亡者愈甚。民間有搜捕之擾，官府有稽考之煩，而邊陲未甞一賴其用。愚以爲沿邊之人驍悍鷙勇，便於弓馬，銳於戰闘，召募而用之，皆爲精兵。今人之所以憚爲兵者何也？以尺籍一定，世世不移，外有死亡之憂，内有侵剋之患。今宜數外別爲尺籍，壯勇是募，優
translation_en:
…first, with Daizhou and Yanmen next. What troubles the frontier inhabitants, they say, is the lack of soldiers, funds, and horses. Yet I humbly believe that all three are available. The troops of Jin and Wei were once the strongest under Heaven, and the young men of Zezhou and Luzhou were also once renowned for their prowess on the frontier. Even today, the mountains and rivers remain intact. Formerly they faced enemies within the Central Kingdom; now they have the support of all under Heaven. Formerly these resources were more than sufficient; now they are insufficient. This is what I cannot understand. Might it simply be that they are not being deployed properly?

Today, along the frontier, men draw bows and discharge whistling arrows, and there are a million armored soldiers. Troops are certainly not lacking, yet frontier officials request reinforcements. Court envoys are dispatched, and measures to find and assemble deserters are extremely strict. Yet there are no locally rooted troops [?]; instead, pampered and physically frail men from the southeast are made to confront the fierce foes of the northwest. Unaccustomed to the climate and water, unfamiliar with the difficult terrain, and without settled quarters, the deserters flee again before they even arrive. The stricter the pursuit, the more serious the desertion becomes. The people suffer the disturbance of searches and arrests, and government offices bear the burden of checking and investigating, yet the frontier has never derived any benefit from their service.

I humbly believe that the people living along the frontier are fierce and valiant, skilled in archery and horsemanship, and eager for combat. If recruited and employed, they would all make excellent soldiers. Why do people today dread becoming soldiers? Because once their names are entered in the military registers, the obligation remains unchanged for generation after generation. On campaign they fear death; within the army they suffer exactions and deductions from their entitlements. Separate military registers should now be established outside the existing quota, recruiting only the strong and brave, and granting preferential …

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
其賞給壯者巳老復募少者補之要有定
數而無定名使其無身後之憂而有望外
賜則人人樂於應募且自戰其山川自
家室與客兵相去又萬萬也而勾詰
之擾可以減矣屯田所以豐財内帑時賜
又所以補其不及也令屯田具在士卒果
得其利名在士卒收在將臣内帑時頒
士沿其賜乎名在士卒𦍑在將臣愚
覈其實而痛懲之沿邊之地可盡
===
收其稅急則出戰緩則入耕以
贍沿邊之人宜可足也而飛輓
省矣太僕行司所以牧馬西蕃
所以補其不及然方養於民民間
爲之擾及給於軍軍中有陪馬之苦
人之所以輕視其馬者凡以爲官而
所有也愚以爲可厚給其直使自市
勿期使過其期是其善牧也不及
不善牧也官勿預知則人不敢輕
punctuated:
其賞給，壯者巳老，復募少者補之，要有定數而無定名，使其無身後之憂而有望外賜，則人人樂於應募。且自戰其山川，自家室，與客兵相去又萬萬也，而勾詰之擾可以減矣。
屯田所以豐財，内帑時賜又所以補其不及也。令屯田具在，士卒果得其利？名在士卒，收在將臣。内帑時頒，士沿其賜乎？名在士卒，𦍑在將臣。愚覈其實而痛懲之。沿邊之地可盡收其稅，急則出戰，緩則入耕，以贍沿邊之人，宜可足也，而飛輓省矣。
太僕行司所以牧馬，西蕃所以補其不及。然方養於民，民間爲之擾；及給於軍，軍中有陪馬之苦。人之所以輕視其馬者，凡以爲官而所有也。愚以爲可厚給其直，使自市。勿期，使過其期，是其善牧也；不及，不善牧也。官勿預知，則人不敢輕。
translation_en:
…their rewards and allowances. When the able-bodied men have grown old, recruit younger men to replace them. The essential point is to maintain a fixed number without permanently fixing the names on the rolls. Give them no cause to worry about what will happen after their deaths, and let them anticipate unexpected rewards; then everyone will gladly enlist. Moreover, they will fight amid their own mountains and rivers and [defend?] their own households. They will differ enormously from troops brought in from elsewhere, and the harassment caused by tracking down and questioning men liable for military service can be reduced.
Military agricultural colonies serve to replenish resources, while occasional grants from the palace treasury make up their shortfalls. The agricultural colonies are all in place [?], but do the soldiers actually receive their benefits? The soldiers are the beneficiaries in name, but the commanding officers collect the proceeds. When palace funds are periodically distributed, do the soldiers receive those grants [?]? Again, the soldiers are the beneficiaries in name, but [the benefits?] remain with the commanding officers [?]. In my humble opinion, the facts should be investigated and the offenders severely punished. Taxes could be collected from all the land along the frontier. In emergencies the men would go out to fight; in quieter times they would return to farming. This should suffice to support the frontier population, and reduce the need for urgent transport of provisions.
The branch Court of the Imperial Stud serves to rear horses, while the western Tibetan regions make up the shortfall. Yet while horses are being raised by the common people, they cause disruption among them; once issued to the army, they impose on the troops the hardship of replacing horses at their own expense [?]. People treat their horses carelessly because they regard them as government property rather than their own [?]. In my humble opinion, they could be given generous funds to buy horses themselves. Do not impose a deadline [?]: if a horse survives beyond its prescribed term, this shows good husbandry; if it fails to reach that term, poor husbandry. Let the authorities refrain from intervening, and people will not dare treat them carelessly…

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
試錄後序
大寶之五年當天下大
附監察御史張〔泰〕來按
援例以白〔泰〕曰㳡
欽予謹㳡之至期
州五州之士試之如故
未迄甲子爰刻所取
氏名與文之中式而
為錄以獻于
司文衡敢無一言為
子者昴哉夫科目
之士由之而出其事重
賢才出而建功植業
企其風采聞望猶泰
punctuated:
試錄後序

大寶之五年，當天下大附，監察御史張〔泰〕來按，援例以白。〔泰〕曰：「㳡欽予謹㳡之。」至期，州五州之士，試之如故。未迄甲子，爰刻所取氏名與文之中式，而為錄，以獻于司文衡。敢無一言為子者昴哉？夫科目之士由之而出，其事重。賢才出而建功植業，企其風采聞望猶泰……
translation_en:
Postface to the Examination Record

In the fifth year of the imperial reign [?], when all under Heaven had rallied in allegiance, Investigating Censor Zhang Tai 張泰 arrived on an inspection tour. Precedent was invoked in making a report. Tai said, “[?] I shall respectfully … [?].” When the appointed time arrived, the scholars of the five subprefectures [?] were examined as before. Before the jiazi day had arrived, the names of those selected and their qualifying compositions were engraved for printing and compiled into a record, to be presented to those charged with judging literary merit. Could I venture to offer no words … [?]?

Men recruited through the examinations emerge by this route; the undertaking is weighty. Worthy and talented men come forth to establish achievements and lasting undertakings. One looks with admiration to their bearing and reputation … [?]

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
矣夫以沿邊之人自戰其地自食
秉其馬其視新至之兵何如也夫
精不在衆兵精則財可省馬可約然
□〔之計不患無馬不患無財不患無〕
〔將耳將得人則統馭有法兵也財〕
〔爲多不得其人則統馭無法〕
馬也以多爲少夫籌邊事之成
之賢否將繫邊之安危也大矣
可不加之意乎故曰患在擇將
謹對
punctuated:
矣。夫以沿邊之人，自戰其地，自食秉其馬，其視新至之兵何如也？夫精不在衆，兵精則財可省，馬可約。然□〔之計，不患無馬，不患無財，不患無〕〔將耳。將得人，則統馭有法，兵也財〕〔爲多；不得其人，則統馭無法〕馬也，以多爲少。夫籌邊事之成，之賢否，將繫邊之安危也，大矣，可不加之意乎？故曰：患在擇將。
謹對。
translation_en:
…Indeed, if the people living along the frontier fight on their own ground and provide their own sustenance and tend their horses [?], how do they compare with troops newly arrived? What matters is quality, not numbers: with select troops, expenditure can be reduced and fewer horses required. Yet □〔in planning …, the concern is not a lack of horses, nor a lack of funds, nor a lack of …〕〔It is the commanders alone [who matter]. If suitable men are appointed as commanders, command and control will be properly ordered; troops and funds …〕〔… count as many [?]; if unsuitable men are appointed, command and control will lack order〕and horses, though numerous, will count as few. Success in planning frontier affairs and the worthiness or otherwise [of those responsible?] will determine the frontier’s security or peril. This is a matter of great importance: can it fail to receive attention? Thus I say: the concern lies in choosing commanders.
Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 弘治五年山西鄉試錄
text:
兹其首善之
山西北也爾諸
厎斯鍾川岳之靈秀
先哲之休風肆掉
蔚皆珊中彪外之文
選矣顧以古之人
而自處其輕且眇
也升對
失其必思天之所
所以用我只重
我猶纖寒之
榮我猶太虛
穀以任之奮
punctuated: 兹其首善之山西北也，爾諸厎斯鍾川岳之靈秀、先哲之休風，肆掉蔚，皆珊中彪外之文選矣。顧以古之人而自處，其輕且眇也。升對，失其必思天之所，所以用我只重。我猶纖寒之榮，我猶太虛，穀以任之奮。
translation_en: …here, its foremost goodness… northern Shanxi [?]. You gentlemen… gather the spiritual excellence of the rivers and mountains and the admirable influence of the sages of former times [?]. Expansively flourishing [?], all are literary selections displaying inner refinement and outward brilliance [?]. Yet, taking the men of antiquity as your measure, you regard yourselves as insignificant and small [?]. Ascending to present a response… losing it [?], you must consider what Heaven… the reason for employing me, and the weight of that responsibility [?]. I am still… slender and poor… honor [?]; I am still like the great void [?]… grain, to undertake it and exert oneself [?]…
